source: The Sun is a star, the closest one to us. Eight planets go around it: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Gravity keeps them in their orbits.
Thinking the Sun is a different kind of thing from the stars. It is a star; other stars look tiny only because they are so much farther away.
Our solar system is the Sun and everything that goes around it: eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets like Pluto, asteroids and comets.

The Sun is a star, a huge ball of hot, glowing gas. The eight planets in order from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune. Gravity keeps them going around the Sun.
The Sun and its planets in order (sizes and distances are not to scale).
The first four are small and rocky. The outer four are giants made mostly of gas or ice. A sentence can help you remember the order: "My Very Eager Mother Just Served Us Noodles."
The Sun looks bigger and brighter than other stars only because it is much closer. Its light takes about 8 minutes to reach us; light from the next nearest star takes over 4 years.
Which planet is fourth from the Sun?
Thinking the Sun is not a star. It is an ordinary star, the closest one to us.
